statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r has no repeated entries, and for every integer d the following are equivalent: (1) there exists j with 0 <= j < len(r) and r[j] = d; (2) 0 <= d < len(security), time <= d, d + time < len(security), for every k with 0 <= k < time, security[d - time + k] >= security[d - time + k + 1], and for every k with 0 <= k < time, security[d + k] <= security[d + k + 1]. The order of the entries of r is irrelevant.
preconditions: security is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(security) <= 10^5 and 0 <= security[t] <= 10^5 for every 0 <= t < len(security); time is a 64-bit integer with 0 <= time <= 10^5.

statement: The function returns a result r (it does not fail) for every security and time satisfying the preconditions.
preconditions: security is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(security) <= 10^5 and 0 <= security[t] <= 10^5 for every 0 <= t < len(security); time is a 64-bit integer with 0 <= time <= 10^5.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, every entry of r is a good day: for every j with 0 <= j < len(r), if d = r[j], then 0 <= d < len(security), time <= d, d + time < len(security), for every k with 0 <= k < time, security[d - time + k] >= security[d - time + k + 1], and for every k with 0 <= k < time, security[d + k] <= security[d + k + 1].
preconditions: security is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(security) <= 10^5 and 0 <= security[t] <= 10^5 for every 0 <= t < len(security); time is a 64-bit integer with 0 <= time <= 10^5.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, every good day appears in r: for every integer d, if 0 <= d < len(security), time <= d, d + time < len(security), for every k with 0 <= k < time, security[d - time + k] >= security[d - time + k + 1], and for every k with 0 <= k < time, security[d + k] <= security[d + k + 1], then there exists j with 0 <= j < len(r) and r[j] = d.
preconditions: security is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(security) <= 10^5 and 0 <= security[t] <= 10^5 for every 0 <= t < len(security); time is a 64-bit integer with 0 <= time <= 10^5.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, r contains no repeated values: for all j and k with 0 <= j < len(r) and 0 <= k < len(r), if r[j] = r[k], then j = k.
preconditions: security is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(security) <= 10^5 and 0 <= security[t] <= 10^5 for every 0 <= t < len(security); time is a 64-bit integer with 0 <= time <= 10^5.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, every entry d of r satisfies time <= d and d + time < len(security). Consequently 0 <= d < len(security), so there are at least time days before d and at least time days after d.
preconditions: security is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(security) <= 10^5 and 0 <= security[t] <= 10^5 for every 0 <= t < len(security); time is a 64-bit integer with 0 <= time <= 10^5.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) <= max(0, len(security) - 2*time).
preconditions: security is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(security) <= 10^5 and 0 <= security[t] <= 10^5 for every 0 <= t < len(security); time is a 64-bit integer with 0 <= time <= 10^5.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, for every j with 0 <= j < len(r), letting d = r[j], for every integer t with 0 <= t < len(security) and d - time <= t and t <= d + time, we have security[d] <= security[t].
preconditions: security is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(security) <= 10^5 and 0 <= security[t] <= 10^5 for every 0 <= t < len(security); time is a 64-bit integer with 0 <= time <= 10^5.

statement: Whenever the function returns a result r, len(r) = 0 if and only if there is no integer d such that 0 <= d < len(security), time <= d, d + time < len(security), for every k with 0 <= k < time, security[d - time + k] >= security[d - time + k + 1], and for every k with 0 <= k < time, security[d + k] <= security[d + k + 1].
preconditions: security is a slice of 64-bit integers with 1 <= len(security) <= 10^5 and 0 <= security[t] <= 10^5 for every 0 <= t < len(security); time is a 64-bit integer with 0 <= time <= 10^5.
